job_title: AI / ML & Full-Stack Software Engineer (Graduate / Entry-Level)
pool_summary: The pool separates into a small research-oriented cluster, a stronger applied-AI/CV cluster, and a broader group with hands-on full-stack product builds. The clearest upper-tail signals are publication-level research output, end-to-end AI artifacts with measurable results, real-time or multi-component product engineering, and international or named-lab exposure.

axes.label: Publication-Level Research Depth
axes.rationale: For an applied AI/ML entry role, demonstrated research output is materially stronger than merely listing machine-learning coursework or participating in a research setting. This axis separates the candidate with peer-reviewed publications from candidates whose research exposure is primarily assistantship or study-based.
axes.strong_criteria: Strong requires active authorship of at least one research publication or equivalent formally disseminated technical research artifact, with the candidate clearly owning the research contribution; two publications in the pool represent the upper benchmark.
axes.moderate_criteria: Moderate requires active research work such as processing an experimental dataset, developing a research model, or serving in a research-assistant role, but without verified publication authorship or a clearly reported research result.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 3/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Measured Applied AI Builds
axes.rationale: The role emphasizes production-oriented AI, computer vision, and predictive systems, so active construction of working AI artifacts with explicit evaluation or recognition performance is more differentiating than generic ML exposure. The pool contains a small set of candidates with concrete classifiers, OCR, ANPR, or recommendation systems.
axes.strong_criteria: Strong requires active ownership of an end-to-end applied AI or computer-vision system with a concrete performance or operational result, such as a classifier reporting 98% accuracy or a functioning OCR/ANPR recognition pipeline; the work must describe what the candidate built rather than only the tool or model used.
axes.moderate_criteria: Moderate requires active ownership of an applied ML, recommendation, OCR, image-processing, or data-processing artifact without a quantified performance result, or active dataset/model work that is technically relevant but narrower than a complete evaluated system.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 5/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Real-Time Product Systems
axes.rationale: Applied AI engineers in this role must integrate models into usable software, making architectural complexity and product execution an important separator from isolated notebooks or simple websites. Real-time communication, workflow systems, multi-component web stacks, and explicit concurrency are the strongest system-building signals in this pool.
axes.strong_criteria: Strong requires active ownership of a multi-component full-stack system with real-time or workflow-oriented architecture, anchored by evidence such as WebSockets or a workflow editor and preferably an explicit operating benchmark such as 100 concurrent users; the candidate must have built the system, not merely supported it.
axes.moderate_criteria: Moderate requires active ownership of a functioning full-stack or mobile product using multiple application layers or integrations, such as a React/Node/Mongo application, booking platform, dashboard, or API-connected app, but without demonstrated real-time complexity or quantified operating scale.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 6/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence

axes.label: Selective Lab Or International Exposure
axes.rationale: The specification explicitly values selective labs and international experience, and this pool contains a distinct subset with university research-lab appointments or overseas academic research exposure. This axis measures the quality and selectivity of the environment itself, independently of whether the candidate produced a publication or shipped a product.
axes.strong_criteria: Strong requires verified participation in an international university research placement or a named university research lab, such as Lakehead University research, HPC/Machine Vision labs, or PakThai/Signal and Machine Learning Lab appointments.
axes.moderate_criteria: Moderate requires a verified academic distinction or research-oriented university placement without the stronger international or named-lab signal, such as a semester exchange passed with distinction or a generic university research internship.
axes.estimated_pool_prevalence: 4/10 candidates show strong or moderate evidence
